name: Tenderhearted Roundedge
description: Judge by eye the angle at which a ring will leave a flat surface before committing the throw.

name: Diskthwack
description: Plant the lead foot and heave the ring hard at a wall so it rebounds toward the target.

name: Hoopedge Carapace
description: Cup the hand low and take the rebounding ring flat against the palm.

name: Hoopglide
description: Reset the feet shoulder-width apart after each rebound so the next throw begins balanced.

name: Grazethwack
description: Bank the ring off a corner so it curves round cover and strikes a foe who thinks himself hidden.

name: Bounceswat
description: Send the ring off two surfaces in turn so it strikes and then comes back to the thrower's hand.

name: Innergrip Curl
description: Stoop after a throw to pick the spent ring from the ground without breaking stride.

name: Attentive Disk
description: Mark where each ring lands by count so none is lost in grass or dust.

name: Harsh Fingerhole
description: Turn the body a half turn and throw sidearm so the ring leaves low and fast.

name: Holeedge Linen
description: Reach into a belt pouch without looking and bring out a fresh ring already turned for the throw.

name: Rigid Outerblade
description: Swing the ring up over the shoulder to knock a blow aside while the other hand reaches for the next.

name: Caromscorer
description: Throw the ring past the target while snatching a second from the belt before the first lands.

name: Gyrateslap
description: Scoop a fallen ring off the ground in an upward cut that tears open the foe's guard.

name: Patient Roundedge
description: Bind the wrist with a firm cloth wrap so repeated throws do not strain the joint.

name: Roundslap
description: Lead the release with the thumb and flick the ring off the forefinger for a short quick throw.

name: Shielding Bladering
description: Fan the open palm across a thrown ring's path to brush it off its line.

name: Diskstalk
description: Step in with the elbow tucked close to the ribs to shorten the arm's swing.

name: Rallying Innergrip
description: Listen for clicks in the wrist as it turns to find where the joint binds.

name: Attentive Outerblade
description: Hold the finished throw pose still for a breath so the wrist learns where a clean release ends.

name: Diskscorer
description: Whip the wrist through a full circle before release so the ring leaves with extra spin and bite.

name: Grazescreen
description: Lock the ring's rim against an enemy blade's guard and twist the wrist to wrench the weapon askew.

name: Tenderhearted Disk
description: Hold two rings in one hand with the rims overlapped so either can be thrown first.

name: Shardgraze
description: Throw one ring at the head and one at the knee in the same breath.

name: Spinrim Carapace
description: Hold a ring flat before the body and take a glancing blow on its broad face.

name: Vapor Spinrim
description: Pull the second ring from its place on the forearm the instant the first leaves the hand.

name: Brawn Ringface
description: Cross one foot over the other to turn the hips and open the line for a second throw.

name: Sound Fingerhole
description: Watch both rings in flight at once to see which one the target moved against.

name: Bounceflog
description: Release two rings a heartbeat apart at different heights so the target cannot guard both.

name: Bouncethwack
description: Cross two rings in flight so their paths meet at the target like the blades of shears.

name: Gall Whirlcut
description: Throw one ring at the guard to pin it high and the second at the exposed ribs below.

name: Cooling Bladering
description: Pick the nearest stone or timber surface that will turn a ring cleanly rather than swallow it.

name: Whirlcut Swat
description: Pitch the ring at a shallow slant so it glances off its first mark and flies on.

name: Roundswat
description: Skip the ring off the top rim of a raised shield and over it into the bearer.

name: Caromswat
description: Hurl the ring down onto a stone floor so it leaps up at knee height.

name: Layered Fingerhole
description: Drop into a low crouch behind the forearm to ride out a wild rebound.

name: Carom Hurdle
description: Back away along the ring's rebound line so it returns toward you rather than past you.

name: Knitting Roundedge
description: Listen to the ring's ping on each surface to tell how much force it kept.

name: Humbounce
description: Strike armor at a slant so the ring caroms off it and cuts the unarmored joint beside it.

name: Pulsegraze
description: Knock the ring off an enemy blade's flat to turn it into the wielder's forearm.

name: Gyrate Hammerfall
description: Bounce one ring off three nearby surfaces in turn so it sweeps a narrow lane of foes.

name: Tenderhearted Ringface
description: Balance the ring on one fingertip and keep it turning level without letting it wander.

name: Sound Bladering
description: Match the finger's flick to the ring's spin so it neither slows nor flies loose.

name: Alert Spinrim
description: Flip the spinning ring from fingertip to palm and close the grip around it.

name: Brutal Bounce
description: Fling the ring from the fingertip mid-turn so it leaves with the spin it already holds.

name: Veering Graze
description: Hop back a pace on both feet while the perched ring keeps its spin undisturbed.

name: Padded Hoopedge
description: Hold a whirling ring on the fingertip as a spinning guard that grinds a blade aside.

name: Wild Carom
description: Let a qi-fed orbit build on the fingertip and fling it all at once for a hard fast cut.

name: Candor Innergrip
description: Sight along the ring's edge with one eye closed to line it up before the throw.

name: Fierce Gyrate
description: Throw the ring edge-on so its thin profile gives a defender little to read.

name: Grim Disk
description: Cast the ring upright like a standing wheel so it slices down the target's centerline.

name: Cooling Ringface
description: Slide the ring home into a leather belt sheath without turning its edge against the hand.

name: Scudding Gyrate
description: Roll the shoulder under a swing and come up with the ring edge turned outward.

name: Hoopedge Buckle
description: Lift a strap-backed forearm so a cutting edge catches on leather and not on skin.

name: Blank Outerblade
description: Hone qi along the rim so an edge-on throw punches through light armor straps.

name: Stern Hoopedge
description: Pass the ring edge-on across a foe at throat height so it shears cloth and leather collars.

name: Poise Fingerhole
description: Fan the ring edge-on before the body to cut thrown darts out of the air.

name: Hoopslap
description: Time the release to the walking stride so the arm swings forward as the lead foot lands.

name: Keen Whirlcut
description: Match the length of the stride to the length of the throw so the ring is not rushed.

name: Sure Ringface
description: Feel which foot carries the weight at release and shift it before the ring leaves.

name: Holeedge Bandage
description: Tuck the ring hand against the hip while running so the edge cannot catch on cloth or bush.

name: Graze Curl
description: Turn on the run and backpedal two paces while the ring hand stays high.

name: Holeedge Barrier
description: Roll away from a swing with the forearm tucked across the face.

name: Rushing Spinrim
description: Throw the ring at the end of a running pivot so body speed adds to its flight.

name: Caromflog
description: Cross the feet mid-stride and sling the ring as the body opens to close the gap while it flies.
